rv.q: It’s a tribute to the novel with modern flair.
Sally Cookson's adaptation is directed by Lily Dyble, who gives the story a dark ferocity.
With a continuously reconfiguring set and a stellar cast, Jane Eyre is a dazzling exploration of forgiveness and resilience.
Dyble's production as a whole is incredible as it intertwines moments of heartache and fear and religious undertones with laughter, friendship, love and musical elements.
While this production is perhaps far less radical than it might have initially seemed on the surface, it is still a nuanced and effective rendition of the classic story.
This version makes a compelling case for revisiting the classics, pairing gothic gloom and dark secrets with bold, inventive theatre.
It’s an inventive and absorbing production, well worth seeing if it comes near you.
It surprised me, kept me guessing and gave me plenty to think about.

cn.t: Critics praise this visceral, atmospheric adaptation for its minimalist staging and modern sensibility that honors Brontë's text while making it feel fresh. Strong performances and Gothic production elements earn consistent acclaim.
